Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speech focus is the clearest for a short presentation?

answer.text: A. I will talk about school.

feedback.text: This is too broad. A clear speech focus names the specific idea the audience should understand.

answer.text: B. School has many different topics.

feedback.text: This is not a focused speaking purpose. It gives a general category but no clear direction.

answer.text: C. Joining a school club can help students make friends and build confidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives one clear idea that can guide the main points of a speech.

answer.text: D. Clubs, lunch, homework, and sports are all important.

feedback.text: This combines unrelated ideas. A coherent speech needs one focus that all points support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

A student is giving a speech about how to prepare for a class presentation. Which order is most logical?

answer.text: A. Practice delivery, choose a topic, create an outline.

feedback.text: This starts near the end of the process. The audience needs the preparation steps in a usable order.

answer.text: B. Create an outline, practice delivery, choose a topic.

feedback.text: This puts outlining before choosing the subject. The topic should come first.

answer.text: C. Practice delivery, create an outline, choose a topic.

feedback.text: This reverses the preparation process. Practice is more effective after the topic and outline are ready.

answer.text: D. Choose a topic, create an outline, practice delivery.

feedback.text: Correct. This order follows the natural process a speaker would use to prepare.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which part of a speech plan best shows that the speaker is following an accepted presentation format?

answer.text: A. Introduction, main points, transitions, and conclusion are clearly labeled.

feedback.text: Correct. These parts show a recognizable speech structure that supports quality presentation.

answer.text: B. The speaker writes every sentence in one long paragraph.

feedback.text: This may hide the structure. A speech format should make the parts easy to see and follow.

answer.text: C. The speaker lists random facts without grouping them.

feedback.text: Random facts do not create an organized presentation format. Ideas need structure.

answer.text: D. The speaker begins with the conclusion and never previews the topic.

feedback.text: This can confuse the audience. Accepted formats usually introduce the focus before developing it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.09

Which transition best connects two points in an organized speech?

answer.text: A. Anyway, here is something else.

feedback.text: This sounds casual and does not explain the connection between ideas.

answer.text: B. After understanding the first benefit, we can also see how this helps students build skills.

feedback.text: Correct. This transition links the previous idea to the next idea and keeps the audience oriented.

answer.text: C. I do not know what to say next.

feedback.text: This weakens delivery and does not guide the audience.

answer.text: D. This has nothing to do with my first point.

feedback.text: This tells the audience the speech is losing focus instead of showing a connection.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L01_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which conclusion best supports coherent focus?

answer.text: A. That is all I found, and there are many other things too.

feedback.text: This ending is vague. A conclusion should bring the audience back to the central idea.

answer.text: B. I also forgot to talk about several unrelated topics.

feedback.text: This introduces new confusion instead of closing the speech.

answer.text: C. School clubs matter because they help students connect, learn, and feel included.

feedback.text: Correct. This conclusion restates the main idea and summarizes the supporting points.

answer.text: D. Lunch schedules should probably change next year.

feedback.text: This shifts to a different topic and breaks the speech focus.
